mainTopic: The rule of דיו: רבי טרפון vs. the חכמים on קרן in רשות הניזק, and when a קל וחומר may be limited
overview: This amud opens in the middle of the משנה. רבי טרפון builds a קל וחומר from רגל to prove that קרן in רשות הניזק pays נזק שלם. The חכמים answer with דיו: a conclusion can't be stronger than its source, so it stays חצי נזק. The גמרא asks how רבי טרפון could reject דיו, since a ברייתא proves it from the Torah with מרים's seven days. It answers that he rejects דיו only where it would leave the קל וחומר teaching nothing. The רבנן and רבי טרפון then argue over the פסוקים about מרים, each reading them to fit his view. רב פפא challenges אביי with a ברייתא about a זב's semen that seems to ignore דיו. אביי shows that דיו there would also cancel the קל וחומר completely. The גמרא then asks which תנא holds that this semen is טמא by carrying, rules out רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, and begins quoting a משנה in כלים that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי טרפון learns Goring from Trampling
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון makes a new קל וחומר: since קרן is stricter than רגל in רשות הרבים, it should also pay in full in רשות הניזק, where רגל pays in full.
steps.simpleTranslation: I won't learn goring from another goring case. I'll learn goring from trampling. In the public area, the Torah was easy on eating and trampling, yet strict on goring. So on the victim's own property, where the Torah was strict on eating and trampling, shouldn't we surely be strict on goring too?
steps.whatsHappening: In the משנה, רבי טרפון offers a fresh קל וחומר to prove that a goring ox in רשות הניזק pays נזק שלם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic: in רשות הרבים, שן and רגל pay nothing, yet קרן pays half, so קרן is the stricter category. In רשות הניזק, שן and רגל pay in full. So the stricter קרן should surely pay in full there too.

keyTerms.meaning: Goring, damage done on purpose by an animal
Trampling, damage done by an animal while walking
Eating, damage done by an animal eating for its own benefit
A 'how much more so' argument from a lighter case to a stricter one

phrases.english: I will not derive Goring from Goring;
I will derive Goring from Trampling:
And if in a place where [the Torah] was lenient
phrases.notes: Here 'lenient' means the owner pays nothing at all for eating and trampling in a public area.

phrases.english: about Eating and Trampling,
in the public domain,
it was strict with Goring;

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶחְמִיר עַל הַשֵּׁן וְעַל הָרֶגֶל,
phrases.english: then a place where it was strict about Eating and Trampling,
on the injured party's property,
is it not logical that we should be strict with Goring?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא אָדוּן קֶרֶן מִקֶּרֶן, אֲנִי אָדוּן קֶרֶן מֵרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's debate. רבי טרפון replaces his earlier argument with a new one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By קל וחומר from רגל, קרן in רשות הניזק should pay נזק שלם.

steps.title: The חכמים answer: it is enough to be like the source
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply with דיו: what comes out of a קל וחומר can be no stronger than its source, so קרן in רשות הניזק pays only חצי נזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: It's enough for the conclusion of a 'how much more so' argument to be equal to its source. Just as goring in the public area pays half damage, so too goring on the victim's property pays half damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי טרפון's קל וחומר using the rule of דיו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They don't deny the logic. They limit how far it can go. His argument starts from the fact that קרן pays half in רשות הרבים, so it can only prove half in רשות הניזק, not full.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is enough': the rule that a קל וחומר's result can't be stronger than its source
The case that comes from the reasoning, meaning the conclusion
The source case being reasoned from
Half the cost of the damage

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of דיו: the result of a קל וחומר can't be stronger than its source. That is why the חכמים hold קרן in רשות הניזק pays only חצי נזק.

phrases.english: They said to him:
It is enough for what comes from the reasoning
to be like the source it was learned from.
Just as in the public domain it is half damage,
so too on the injured party's property it is half damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects how far רבי טרפון's קל וחומר can reach.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the result (נזק שלם), not the logic of the קל וחומר itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The conclusion goes beyond its source, which only pays חצי נזק.

steps.title: How can רבי טרפון reject a Torah rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: how can רבי טרפון not accept דיו, when דיו comes from the Torah?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does רבי טרפון really not accept 'it is enough'? But 'it is enough' comes from the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by attacking רבי טרפון's position, claiming דיו is a Torah-level rule that no one should reject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי טרפון insisted on נזק שלם, he seems to reject דיו altogether. The גמרא says that can't be right, because דיו is דאורייתא. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
He does not hold of / accept

phrases.english: Gemara
And Rabbi Tarfon does not accept 'it is enough'?!
But 'it is enough' is from the Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the משנה and questions רבי טרפון's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי טרפון's apparent rejection of דיו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דיו is a Torah rule, so no תנא could reject it.

steps.title: Proof from מרים's seven days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows דיו in the Torah: by קל וחומר, מרים should have been sent out fourteen days for the שכינה's anger, yet she got only seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: How do we see a 'how much more so' argument? 'And ה׳ said to משה: If her father had spit in her face, would she not be ashamed seven days?' By 'how much more so', for ה׳'s anger it should be fourteen days! But it's enough for the conclusion to be like its source.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its challenge, showing that the Torah itself uses דיו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's anger brings seven days of shame. ה׳'s anger should bring more, maybe fourteen. Yet מרים was sent out for only seven, which shows the Torah limits the result to the source: דיו.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
From a 'how much more so' argument, how so?
"And ה׳ said to Moshe:
If her father had spit in her face,
would she not be ashamed seven days?!"

phrases.aramaic: קַל וְחוֹמֶר לַשְּׁכִינָה, אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם!
phrases.english: By 'how much more so', for the Divine Presence: fourteen days!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן.
phrases.english: Rather, it is enough for what comes from the reasoning to be like its source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim that דיו is דאורייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That דיו is a Torah-level rule
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on במדבר 12:14, the seven days of מרים

steps.title: רבי טרפון rejects דיו only when it cancels the whole argument
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון does accept דיו in general. He rejects it only where it would leave the קל וחומר teaching nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he doesn't accept 'it is enough', that's where it would break the 'how much more so' argument completely. Where it doesn't break the argument, he does accept 'it is enough'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its challenge by drawing a line: רבי טרפון accepts דיו, except where it would cancel the קל וחומר entirely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer suggests that in the משנה's case, דיו would bring the result back to just חצי נזק and the קל וחומר would add nothing. In such a case רבי טרפון says the קל וחומר wins. Where the קל וחומר still teaches something after דיו, he agrees to דיו.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי טרפון rejects דיו altogether. He fully accepts it as a Torah rule. He only says it can't wipe out the whole קל וחומר.

phrases.english: When he does not accept 'it is enough',
it is where it knocks out the 'how much more so' argument;
phrases.notes: He means a case where using דיו would leave the קל וחומר teaching nothing at all.

phrases.english: where it does not knock out the 'how much more so' argument,
he does accept 'it is enough'.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי לֵית לֵיהּ דַּיּוֹ הֵיכָא דְּמִפְּרִיךְ קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 by limiting רבי טרפון's rejection of דיו.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי טרפון rejects דיו completely, against the Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי טרפון accepts דיו, except where it would cancel the קל וחומר entirely.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the key rule for the rest of the sugya: the debate is about whether the קל וחומר has anything left to teach after דיו.

steps.title: Why מרים's case still teaches something
steps.stepSummary: With מרים, seven days for the שכינה's anger aren't written. The קל וחומר brings fourteen, דיו cuts it to seven, and the seven days are still a new teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with מרים, seven days for ה׳'s anger aren't written. The 'how much more so' came and brought fourteen. 'It is enough' came and took away seven, and left seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies its answer to the ברייתא, showing that with מרים, דיו doesn't cancel the קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only gives seven days for a father's anger. It says nothing about the שכינה. So even after דיו cuts fourteen down to seven, the קל וחומר still taught the seven days for the שכינה, and רבי טרפון agrees there.
steps.whatToRemember: דיו trims a קל וחומר but doesn't erase it: with מרים, fourteen became seven, and the seven still came from the קל וחומר. רבי טרפון objects only where nothing would be left.

phrases.english: There (with Miriam),
seven days for the Divine Presence are not written;
the 'how much more so' came and brought fourteen,
'it is enough' came and removed seven,
and left seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the distinction of step 5 to the מרים proof of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the distinction to the cited source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מרים case proves רבי טרפון must accept דיו even in the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: With מרים, the קל וחומר still taught seven days, so it was not cancelled, and the case is no proof against רבי טרפון.

steps.title: With קרן, דיו would leave the קל וחומר teaching nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון contrasts מרים with קרן. For קרן, חצי נזק is already written, so דיו would cancel the קל וחומר completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, half damage is already written in the Torah. The קל וחומר comes and adds another half, making full damage. If you apply דיו, the קל וחומר is left with nothing to teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי טרפון's answer by showing how the case of קרן is different from מרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For קרן, the Torah already says חצי נזק, so the only thing the קל וחומר adds is the second half. If דיו cuts the payment back to half, the קל וחומר teaches nothing new at all. In that kind of case, רבי טרפון does not apply דיו.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is enough": what comes from a קל וחומר can be no stronger than its source
It is knocked down; here, left with nothing to teach

steps.whyThisMatters: This defines רבי טרפון's whole position. He accepts דיו only as long as it does not leave the קל וחומר teaching nothing.

phrases.english: But here, half damage is written;
phrases.notes: "Here" means קרן. The Torah already says it pays half.

phrases.english: and the קל וחומר comes and brings

phrases.aramaic: חֲצִי נֶזֶק אַחֲרִינָא, וְנַעֲשָׂה נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם;
phrases.english: another half damage, making it full damage;
if you apply דיו,
the קל וחומר is cancelled!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast begun in step 6 by explaining the קרן side.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מרים proves that דיו always applies, so רבי טרפון should apply it to קרן too.
steps.terutzMaskana: With קרן, דיו would leave the קל וחומר teaching nothing, so רבי טרפון does not apply it there.

steps.title: The רבנן say מרים's seven days are written openly
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reject רבי טרפון's distinction. The seven days are stated in the פסוק, so with מרים too, דיו left the קל וחומר teaching nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They hold that the seven days for the שכינה's anger are written: "Let her be shut up seven days."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן answer רבי טרפון. They say the seven days are actually written in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seven days are already written, then the קל וחומר could only have added the extra seven. Once דיו cut those away, the קל וחומר taught nothing. So according to the רבנן, מרים proves that דיו applies even when it cancels the קל וחומר completely.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים who argue with רבי טרפון
Let her be shut out (sent outside the camp)

phrases.english: And the רבנן? The seven days of the שכינה are written:
"Let her be shut up seven days."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 6's claim that the seven days are not written.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי טרפון's reading of the מרים case, which his distinction depends on.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The claim that the seven days are not written is wrong, because the פסוק states them.

steps.title: רבי טרפון says that פסוק is the source for דיו
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון explains that "תסגר שבעת ימים" is not a separate statement of seven days. It is the Torah telling us to apply דיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי טרפון? That word "תסגר" is there to teach us that we apply דיו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי טרפון's answer to the רבנן: the פסוק they quoted is itself the lesson of דיו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי טרפון, the פסוק does not give the seven days independently. It is the Torah's way of saying "apply דיו to the קל וחומר." So the seven days still come from the קל וחומר, and the קל וחומר is not left empty.

phrases.english: And רבי טרפון? That "Let her be shut up"
is there to teach that we apply דיו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's argument from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the purpose of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק states the seven days on its own, so the קל וחומר teaches nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is the source of דיו, and the seven days still come through the קל וחומר.

steps.title: The רבנן point to a second פסוק about מרים
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן note that another פסוק, "ותסגר מרים," also mentions the seven days. So the seven days are still written somewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? Another פסוק is written: "And מרים was shut up."
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן push back: even if one פסוק teaches דיו, a second פסוק also says the seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "תסגר" teaches דיו, then "ותסגר מרים" would be the one that states the seven days openly. That brings back the רבנן's point: the seven days are written, and still the קל וחומר was cut down by דיו.

phrases.english: And the רבנן? Another פסוק is written:
"And מרים was shut up."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 9 with an extra פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי טרפון's claim that the seven days are not written independently
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if one פסוק teaches דיו, the second פסוק states the seven days. So the קל וחומר still ended up teaching nothing.

steps.title: The second פסוק teaches that דיו applies everywhere
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון says the second פסוק teaches that דיו applies in all cases. Otherwise you might think it applied to מרים only because of משה's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי טרפון? That פסוק teaches that we apply דיו even in general. Don't say that here it was because of משה's honor, but in general we don't apply it. The פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי טרפון's final answer: the second פסוק has its own job, so the seven days are still not stated on their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the second פסוק, someone might think מרים's punishment was cut down only out of respect for משה. The extra פסוק teaches that דיו is a general rule for every קל וחומר. Each פסוק has a different job, so רבי טרפון's distinction stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: In general, in all other cases
So that you should not say

steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון accepts דיו as a general Torah rule, but not when it would leave the קל וחומר teaching nothing, as with קרן in רשות הניזק. The רבנן apply דיו even then. Both sides read the פסוקים about מרים to fit their view.

phrases.english: And רבי טרפון? That one
teaches that even in general we apply דיו,
so that you should not say: here
it was because of the honor of משה,
but in general we do not;
the פסוק teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן, הָהוּא – דַּאֲפִילּוּ בְּעָלְמָא דָּרְשִׁינַן דַּיּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second-פסוק challenge from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving the extra פסוק its own lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דיו applied to מרים only out of respect for משה.
steps.terutzMaskana: דיו is a general rule, and the seven days are still not stated on their own.

steps.title: רב פפא: Here is a תנא who ignores the rule of דיו
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי: there is a תנא who does not apply דיו, even in a case where דיו would not cancel the קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But there is this תנא who does not use דיו, even though here דיו would not knock down the קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a challenge against the idea that everyone accepts דיו when it leaves the קל וחומר with something to teach. He is setting up a proof from a ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the argument was only about cases where דיו would make the קל וחומר useless. רב פפא claims he has found a תנא who skips דיו even when it would leave the קל וחומר with something to teach. If he is right, then not everyone holds of דיו.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is enough': the result of a קל וחומר cannot be stricter than its source
A sage of the משנה or ברייתא period
Knocks down, cancels (here: cancels the קל וחומר)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הַאי תַּנָּא, דְּלָא דָּרֵישׁ דַּיּוֹ,
phrases.english: But there is this tanna who does not apply 'it is enough,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מִפְּרִיךְ קַל וָחוֹמֶר!
phrases.english: even though here it would not cancel the kal vachomer!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: וְהָא הַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind the רבי טרפון and רבנן discussion that everyone applies דיו where it does not cancel the קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that every תנא applies דיו whenever doing so leaves the קל וחומר with something to teach.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תנא is found who does not limit his קל וחומר with דיו, even though limiting it would still leave it useful.

steps.title: The ברייתא: a קל וחומר for the semen of a זב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns the טומאה of a זב's קרי through a קל וחומר from spittle.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: From where do we know that a זב's קרי is טמא? It is logical. Spittle is טהור from a טהור person, yet it is טמא from a טמא person (a זב). Then קרי, which is טמא even from a טהור person, should surely be טמא in the stronger way when it comes from a טמא person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that רב פפא uses as his proof. It is a קל וחומר comparing spittle with קרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spittle starts out טהור, yet from a זב it becomes טמא in the strong way of the זב's own discharges. קרי is already טמא from a regular person, so from a זב it should be at least as severe. 'טמא בטמא' means the strong טומאה of a זב, which applies even through carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with a gonorrhea-like discharge, who has a severe טומאה
'It is logical': introduces a קל וחומר

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
The semen of a zav, from where do we know it is impure?
It is a logical derivation:
Just as what is pure from a pure person is impure from an impure person;
phrases.notes: This is spit: it's טהור from an ordinary person, but from a זב it's טמא.

phrases.english: what is impure even from a pure person,
phrases.notes: This is קרי, which is טמא even from someone who is otherwise טהור.

phrases.english: is it not logical that it should be impure from an impure person?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text for רב פפא's challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That this תנא does not apply דיו.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא deriving the טומאה of a זב's קרי through a קל וחומר from spittle.

steps.title: Why didn't the תנא limit it to touching?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא applies the קל וחומר to both מגע and משא. דיו could have limited it to מגע, so his not doing so shows he rejects דיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא applies it to both touching and carrying. Why? Let us say the קל וחומר works for touching, and דיו works to exclude carrying!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא spells out exactly why the ברייתא is a problem. The תנא should have used דיו to stop the result at touching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular קרי (the source) is טמא only by touching, not by carrying. With דיו, the קל וחומר would teach that a זב's קרי is טמא by touching, and nothing more. That would still teach something, so it would not be canceled. Since the תנא includes carrying too, he seems to ignore דיו completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Becoming טמא by carrying, even without touching

steps.confusionAlert: Regular קרי is טמא by touching but NOT by carrying. That is why דיו would cut off the carrying part.

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא מַיְיתֵי לַהּ בֵּין לְמַגָּע בֵּין לְמַשָּׂא.
phrases.english: And he brings it both for contact and for carrying.
But why?
Let us say: the kal vachomer is effective for contact,
and 'it is enough' is effective to exclude carrying!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָא מַיְיתֵי לַהּ בֵּין לְמַגָּע בֵּין לְמַשָּׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that all תנאים apply דיו when it does not cancel the קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דיו would leave the קל וחומר teaching מגע, yet the תנא extends it to משא. So he does not apply דיו.

steps.title: Blocking the defense that touching needs no קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא anticipates a reply: touching is obvious, so the קל וחומר only teaches carrying. He rejects it, because a פסוק might have suggested a זב's קרי is not טמא at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the קל וחומר is not needed for touching, because a זב's קרי is surely no less than a טהור man's, that is wrong. It is needed. I might have thought that since it says 'מקרה לילה,' only a man whose קרי comes from his own nature is טמא. A זב is excluded, because something else (his illness) caused it. So the קל וחומר teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a possible defense of the תנא and knocks it down himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense: if touching is obvious, the קל וחומר exists only to teach carrying, and דיו would wipe it out completely. רב פפא answers that touching is not obvious, because 'מקרה לילה' might exclude a זב. So the קל וחומר is needed for touching, and his challenge stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: introduces a possible reply
Is not worse or less than
It would enter your mind (a mistaken first thought)

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: לְמַגָּע לָא אִצְטְרִיךְ קַל וָחוֹמֶר,
phrases.english: And if you would say: for contact the kal vachomer is not needed,
since it is no less than the semen of a pure man;
it is needed, for it would enter your mind to say:
'Happens to him by night' is written,
meaning one whose own emission brought it on;

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא זֶה, שֶׁאֵין קִרְיוֹ גּוֹרֵם לוֹ –
phrases.english: excluding this one, whose emission did not bring it on,
but rather something else caused it;
phrases.notes: The 'something else' is his זב condition.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: לְמַגָּע לָא אִצְטְרִיךְ קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 14 by shutting down a likely answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested defense that the קל וחומר is needed only for משא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Touching is not obvious, since 'מקרה לילה' could be read to exclude a זב, whose קרי comes from his illness.

steps.title: אביי: The verse never says 'not something else'
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the פסוק does not exclude a זב, so touching is already known. The קל וחומר is needed only for carrying, and דיו would cancel it completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it say 'and not something else'?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רב פפא's reading of the פסוק. This defends the idea that every תנא applies דיו at least wherever it would still leave the קל וחומר something to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מקרה לילה' does not say 'only from his own nature,' so a זב's קרי is טמא by touching straight from the פסוק. The קל וחומר's only job is carrying. If דיו stopped it at touching, it would teach nothing, so the תנא is right not to apply דיו. The ברייתא is no proof against דיו.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...?! (a rhetorical 'it does not say that')
Something else (here: a different cause, like illness)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about a זב's קרי does not prove anyone rejects דיו. Touching comes from the פסוק itself, and the קל וחומר is needed only for carrying, where דיו would cancel it completely.

phrases.english: Is it written 'and not something else'?!
phrases.notes: This is אביי's reply. The פסוק never excludes a זב, so touching is already known from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns רב פפא's rejection in step 15, which answers the challenge of steps 12 and 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק so the קל וחומר is needed only for משא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מקרה לילה' excludes a זב, so the קל וחומר is needed for touching, and דיו could have limited it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק does not exclude a זב. Touching is known from it, and דיו would cancel the קל וחומר completely, so the תנא does not apply it.

steps.title: Who holds that a זב's semen is טמא by carrying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that the שכבת זרע of a זב makes things טמא through משא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא you heard say that the semen of a זב makes things טמא by carrying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask a side question: whose opinion is it that a זב's שכבת זרע is טמא even by carrying? This sets up the search that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 13-16 relied on a ברייתא that gives a זב's semen טומאה by carrying. Now the גמרא wants to find out which known תנא actually holds that view.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with a specific impure discharge, which makes him a source of טומאה
Carrying, moving something without touching it, which can still pass on טומאה

phrases.english: And who is the תנא that you heard say:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע שֶׁל זָב מְטַמְּאָה בְּמַשָּׂא?
phrases.english: The semen of a זב makes things טמא by carrying?
phrases.notes: This is the view of the ברייתא from Steps 13-14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question coming out of the ברייתא discussed in Steps 13-16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a זב's שכבת זרע is טמא through משא

steps.title: Not רבי אליעזר and not רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is neither רבי אליעזר nor רבי יהושע, and brings their argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not רבי אליעזר and not רבי יהושע. As we learned: a זב's semen makes things טמא by touching but not by carrying, says רבי אליעזר. רבי יהושע says it also makes things טמא by carrying, because it always comes out together with tiny drops of זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the opinion does not belong to either רבי אליעזר or רבי יהושע. It quotes their argument to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר clearly says there is no טומאה by carrying. רבי יהושע does say there is, but he gives a different reason: the semen is mixed with drops of זיבה, which is טמא by carrying anyway. The next step explains why that means he is not our תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Touching, passing on טומאה through contact

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע does say the semen is טמא by carrying, so it looks like he IS the answer. But his reason is the drops of זיבה, not the semen itself, as the next step explains.

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: Not רבי אליעזר, and not רבי יהושע.
As we learned: the semen of a זב
makes things טמא by touching,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְטַמְּאָה בְּמַשָּׂא; דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.english: but does not make things טמא by carrying; these are the words of רבי אליעזר.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: אַף מְטַמְּאָה בְּמַשָּׂא,
phrases.english: And רבי יהושע says: it also makes things טמא by carrying,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּלֹא צִחְצוּחֵי זִיבָה.
phrases.english: because it is impossible without tiny drops of זיבה.
phrases.notes: He means the semen always comes out with a little זיבה in it, and זיבה itself is טמא by carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17 in the negative, with a source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Neither רבי אליעזר nor רבי יהושע holds that the semen itself is טמא by carrying

steps.title: Why רבי יהושע is not the answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that רבי יהושע gives טומאה by carrying only because of the drops of זיבה; without them, he would agree there is none.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע only said it there because it always comes with drops of זיבה. Otherwise, no, it would not be טמא by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהושע does not count as the תנא it is looking for. His reason has nothing to do with a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's טומאה by carrying comes only from the mixed-in זיבה. That means the semen alone would not be טמא by carrying even for him. So both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree with the ברייתא that used a קל וחומר to make the semen itself טמא by carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said this (in that specific case)

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם –
phrases.english: רבי יהושע only said there

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּלֹא צִחְצוּחֵי זִיבָה,
phrases.english: because it is impossible without tiny drops of זיבה,
but if not for this, it would not!

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי יהושע, quoted in Step 18, is not the answer
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע does not hold the semen itself is טמא by carrying
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's own reason: the drops of זיבה

steps.title: The answer is a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to name the real source: the תנא of a משנה that lists levels of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is this תנא, as we learned: 'Higher than these...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to bring the תנא who does hold this view. This is a setup line; the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having ruled out רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, the גמרא turns to a משנה that ranks sources of טומאה from lighter to heavier. The words 'higher than these' open the next level of that list.

keyTerms.meaning: Higher than them (a more severe level)

phrases.english: Rather, it is this תנא,
as we learned: higher than them
phrases.notes: This is from the list of טומאות in כלים 1:3. 'Them' means the lighter טומאות listed just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out the two תנאים, begins to bring the right source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא of the משנה in כלים that ranks levels of טומאה (continues on the next amud)
